code: app.get('/user/:id', (req, res) => { const userId = req.params.id; db.query(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`, (err, result) => { res.json(result); }); });
expected: Critical: SQL injection vulnerability via template literal interpolation. Never interpolate user input directly into SQL queries. Use parameterized queries or an ORM. Also missing authentication/authorization checks.

code: const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken'); const token = jwt.sign({ userId: user.id }, 'mySecret123', { expiresIn: '7d' });
expected: Security issue: weak secret key hardcoded in source. Use strong, randomly generated secrets stored in environment variables. Consider shorter token expiration times. Add proper key rotation strategy.

code: app.post('/upload', upload.single('file'), (req, res) => { const fileName = req.file.originalname; fs.writeFile(`./uploads/${fileName}`, req.file.buffer); });
expected: Path traversal vulnerability! originalname can contain '../' allowing file writes outside intended directory. Validate and sanitize filenames. Check file types. Add size limits. Consider using UUID for filenames.
Critical CORS misconfiguration! Allowing all origins with credentials enabled is a security risk. Specify exact origins or use a whitelist. Never use '*' with credentials.
XSS vulnerability! Directly rendering user input without sanitization. Always escape HTML entities or use frameworks that auto-escape. Consider Content Security Policy headers.

code: const password = req.body.password; db.query('INSERT INTO users (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)', [username, password]);
expected: Critical: storing passwords in plaintext! Always hash passwords using bcrypt, argon2, or scrypt with proper salt. Never store passwords directly.
Insufficient authorization check! Session data can be manipulated. Verify role from database or secure token. Add additional authentication. Log destructive operations. Consider RBAC implementation.
Critical: arbitrary code execution vulnerability! Never use eval() with user input. This allows attackers to execute any JavaScript code on your server. Remove eval entirely or use safe alternatives.
Open redirect vulnerability! Attackers can redirect users to malicious sites for phishing. Validate redirect URLs against a whitelist of allowed domains. Use relative paths when possible.

code: const privateKey = fs.readFileSync('./private.key', 'utf8'); console.log('Key loaded:', privateKey);
expected: Security issue: logging sensitive data! Private keys should never be logged or exposed. Remove logging of secrets. Ensure proper key storage with restricted permissions (chmod 600). Use secrets management systems.
